waterSolubility: ~113 g/L at 20 °C (dissolves to form sulfurous acid H₂SO₃)
environmentalPersistence: Low to moderate — atmospheric half-life ~1–2 weeks via oxidation to SO₃/H₂SO₄

morphologicalEffects.leafCurl: Moderate to strong — SO₂ entry via stomata causes immediate mesophyll damage and structural collapse
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Strong — SO₂ dissolves to sulfurous acid in mesophyll; H⁺ bleaches chlorophyll
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Moderate-strong — interveinal necrosis characteristic; bleached interveinal zones progressing to brown
morphologicalEffects.rootGrowth: Minimally affected — primarily a foliar gas
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Older mature leaves most sensitive; very young leaves partially protected by closed stomata

physiologyEffects.chlorophyllReduction: Strong — acid dissolution of mesophyll and direct chlorophyll bleaching
physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Strongly reduced — SO₂ is one of the strongest abiotic stomatal closure inducers known

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Strong — sulfite radical (SO₃•⁻) is highly reactive; direct DNA and protein damage

microbiomeEffects.diversityReduction: Moderate — primarily foliar effects; some rhizosphere impact via acid leachate

temporalDynamics.recoveryTime: Poor for necrotic tissue; stomatal function can partially recover if exposure stops
temporalDynamics.acclimation: Partial — sulfite oxidase activity can increase with sub-lethal exposure

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Green → pale interveinal bleaching → brown interveinal necrosis; veins remain green longer
visualSimulation.damageSpread: Interveinal zones first, veins last — distinctive acid rain visual signature
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Interveinal necrosis/bleaching with green veins — most diagnostically distinctive pattern of the acid rain group
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Moderate — S-sulfonated glutathione and sulfate signature
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: Interveinal zones remain scarred; vein-delimited recovery if exposure stops

synergies.synergyNote: SO₂ + NO₂ is the core acid rain precursor pair — together they produce both H₂SO₄ and HNO₃ atmospheric deposition. SO₂ + ozone is especially damaging: ozone opens stomata while SO₂ enters through them.

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Coal combustion, oil refining, smelting of sulfide ores, volcanic eruptions — largest anthropogenic source is coal power plants
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Used as preservative in dried fruits and wine (E220); also soil fumigant historically
educationalContext.humanToxicity: High — severe respiratory irritant; triggers asthma attacks; WHO standard: 20 µg/m³ 24-hour mean
educationalContext.climateLink: SO₂ emissions create sulfate aerosols that actually cool climate (masking warming from CO₂) — the 'sulfate aerosol masking' problem means reducing coal burning could temporarily accelerate warming
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Primarily outdoor; indoor near volcanic areas
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: The sulfate aerosol paradox — cleaning up SO₂ pollution actually makes climate change temporarily worse. One of the most counterintuitive climate science facts.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Acid rain, respiratory health, sulfate aerosol climate masking, coal power
